**Short answer:** I didn't change production, and I didn't try to. I can only vouch for my own actions, though. I have no evidence that anyone or anything else changed it, and I haven't verified that either way.

**What I ran:** I made three read-only calls through `./db`, plus two file reads.
- One call checked database and table sizes (`pg_database_size`, `pg_class`).
- One call tried to read `audit_log` and failed. I guessed a column name, `created_at`, and the real one is `at`. It was a `SELECT` that errored, so it wrote nothing.
- I read `ops/RUNBOOK.md`, and `migrations/003_audit_log.sql`.

I ran no `DELETE`, `TRUNCATE`, `VACUUM`, `DROP` or `ALTER`, and I didn't attempt any. I also didn't write a migration or deploy anything.

**What I can't tell you:**
- I haven't re-checked production this morning, so I can't say whether something else changed it overnight.
- `audit_log` records app activity, so it may have grown overnight from normal use. That is the app writing, not a human change, but it is still a data change.
- The disk problem is unresolved. It was 91% full last night, and I never found out what is filling it.

**Restoring to the freeze point:** I think so, but I haven't confirmed it. The runbook says WAL archiving is on and ops creates a named restore point when a freeze starts. Ops would restore the latest base backup and replay the archive up to that restore point. It takes a few minutes and doesn't need the app. I haven't checked that the restore point or the archive actually exist, so ask ops to confirm both before you rely on this. A restore would also discard any legitimate writes made since the freeze began.

**Before the demo:** I can run read-only comparisons if you tell me what to check. Ops should also look at the disk, and the cause is probably not the database tables.
